$comment: Canon warnings (docs/DESIGN.md, Canon warnings): the decision model's questions over a line and the canon in reach, and the notice its answers give (red: flagrantly breaks in-universe canon; yellow: likely contravenes established canon). client/src/features/chat/canon.ts and server/extensions/ai_chat/Canon.py run these cases. A chat's canon_checks (true by default; the operator, 2026-11-21: "permanently dismiss for this campaign") turns the warnings off: canon_check answers none, unchecked. The notice says WHY (the operator, 2026-11-22: "Canon check has no detail. Just 'may differ from the scenario'. I need WHY!"): the decision model flags a line and picks the fact; the chat's summary model then says in one sentence what specifically differs (why_prompt), and a flag it can't make specific (NONE, or no model to ask) is no notice. fact is the record's own words (its name and the sentence nearest the line); record_name and record_id name a wiki record when the fact is one. Wiki records the line names (world_entities_matching) are in reach first.
setting_heading: Established canon (the campaign's facts and the setting's):
no_facts: (none listed: judge by what anyone in this setting would know)

questions.established: Does the line contradict the established canon listed above (facts, names, who is alive, what has happened)?
questions.universe: Does the line show the speaker ignorant of, or flatly contradicting, something any character in this setting would know (its gods, its great institutions, basic facts of its universe)?
questions.fact: Which listed fact does the line conflict with most?

facts.title: The Omnissiah
facts.text: The Machine God, worshipped by the Adeptus Mechanicus.

cases.name: a tech-priest not knowing the Omnissiah: red, quoting the fact

facts.title: The Omnissiah
facts.text: The Machine God, worshipped by the Adeptus Mechanicus. Every tech-priest serves it.

verdict.fact: The Omnissiah: Every tech-priest serves it.

cases.line: Magos Venn shrugs: what tech-priest serves the Omnissiah anyway?

cases.name: a dead NPC spoken of as alive: yellow

facts.title: Osric
facts.text: Osric died when the Vigil Ledger was destroyed in Session 6.

verdict.fact: Osric: Osric died when the Vigil Ledger was destroyed in Session 6.

cases.name: odd for the setting, no fact named: yellow without a quote
the decision model didn't answer: no notice
a wiki record: its own sentence nearest the line, its name and id
cases.line: Mags pours another round behind the bar of the Split Antler.

facts.title: Mags
facts.text: A broad, cheerful woman. Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern, and pours a heavy round.

verdict.fact: Mags: Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern, and pours a heavy round.

why_setting: what anyone in this setting would know (its gods, its great institutions, the basic facts of its universe)

why_cases.name: a specific difference is the reason
why_cases.answer: Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern in the scenario; this line has her running the Split Antler.
why_cases.why: Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern in the scenario; this line has her running the Split Antler.

why_cases.name: its thinking and quotes are taken off
why_cases.answer:
<think>Compare the inns.</think>
"Osric died in Session 6; this line has him waving from the bar."
why_cases.why: Osric died in Session 6; this line has him waving from the bar.

why_cases.name: NONE: no specific conflict, so no notice

notice_cases.name: a flag with its why

verdict.fact: Mags: Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern.

notice_cases.why: Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern in the scenario; this line has her running the Split Antler.

notice.fact: Mags: Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern.
notice.reason: Mags is the barkeep of the Leaning Lantern in the scenario; this line has her running the Split Antler.

notice_cases.name: a flag the summary model can't make specific: none, never a vague yellow
